title: Runes in 10 Minutes
audience: Anyone new to Runes who wants an accurate, hype-free mental model.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with Bitcoin transactions and UTXOs.
outcomes: Explain how runestones live in Bitcoin outputs, how balances move, and why cenotaphs exist.

lessons.title: UTXOs, Not Account Balances
lessons.summary: Rune units are held by Bitcoin outpoints. Spending an outpoint spends its runes.

lessons.title: The Carrier Script
lessons.summary: OP_RETURN OP_13 identifies the runestone. All data pushes concatenate into the payload.

lessons.title: The Four Lifecycle Events
lessons.summary: Etch, mint, transfer, and burn: the four operations in the protocol.

lessons.title: Cenotaphs and Upgrade Safety
lessons.summary: Malformed messages burn balances rather than misallocating them.

quiz.question: Where are rune balances stored on Bitcoin?
options: In a global smart contract account
On transaction outpoints (UTXOs), alongside satoshis
Inside the OP_RETURN script itself
In an offchain database operated by miners
quiz.explanation: Rule R44 states that balances are per rune, per outpoint. The OP_RETURN runestone carries instructions, not a vault.

quiz.question: What happens if a runestone contains a malformed field producing a cenotaph?
options: The Bitcoin transaction is rejected by miners
All input runes in the transaction are burned
The invalid field is skipped and remaining edicts execute
Runes automatically return to the sender
quiz.explanation: Rule R45 states that in a cenotaph transaction, every input rune balance and every minted or premined amount is burned.

title: Inspect a Runestone Safely
audience: Users, operators, and analysts verifying raw scripts before signing or indexing.
prerequisites: Understanding of hex encoding and Bitcoin script opcodes.
outcomes: Dissect carrier scripts byte by byte, extract varints, decode tags, and identify flaws.

lessons.title: Finding the Runestone in a Transaction
lessons.summary: Search outputs in order for OP_RETURN OP_13; the first match controls.

lessons.title: Payload Push Opcodes
lessons.summary: Distinguish pushdata opcodes from non-pushdata opcodes that trigger flaw Opcode.

lessons.title: LEB128 Varint Decoding
lessons.summary: Decode up to 19 bytes per integer, observing the 19th-byte overflow mask.

lessons.title: Tag Queue Consumption
lessons.summary: Observe how even tags require full consumption while odd tags degrade silently.

quiz.question: What opcode sequence starts an authentic Runes carrier script?
options: 0x6a 0x5d (OP_RETURN OP_13)
quiz.explanation: Rule R1 specifies OP_RETURN (0x6a) followed immediately by OP_13 (0x5d).

title: Transfer Runes Safely
audience: Users and wallet integrators sending or batching rune balances.
outcomes: Construct edicts, handle delta encoding, avoid change loss, and calculate splits safely.

lessons.title: Edict Quadruple Anatomy
lessons.summary: Block delta, tx delta/index, amount, and output index.

lessons.title: Delta Encoding Mechanics
lessons.summary: How accumulating block and transaction deltas saves payload bytes.

lessons.title: The Output 0 Default Footgun
lessons.summary: Why unallocated runes go to the first non-OP_RETURN output unless a pointer directs them.

lessons.title: Sweeps and Splits
lessons.summary: Amount 0 sweeps remaining balance; output equal to output count splits.

quiz.question: Where do unallocated runes go if no pointer is specified?
options: They are permanently burned
They go to the first non-OP_RETURN spendable output
They stay on the input outpoint
They are split among all outputs
quiz.explanation: Rule R39 and R42 state that without a pointer, unallocated runes go to the first non-OP_RETURN output.

title: Understand and Evaluate a Mint
audience: Users evaluating mint eligibility and developers building mint checkers.
prerequisites: Familiarity with block height and transaction indexing.
outcomes: Calculate effective mint start and end windows, evaluate caps, and detect silent mint failures.

lessons.title: Tag 20 Mint Pair
lessons.summary: Mint tag requires exactly two values: target block and tx index.

lessons.title: Window Intersection Rules
lessons.summary: Start is the maximum of absolute and offset bounds; end is the minimum.

lessons.title: Exclusive End Height
lessons.summary: Minting at the exact end height is closed and fails.

lessons.title: Silent Failure Semantics
lessons.summary: An invalid or closed mint does not error or burn: it produces nothing.

quiz.question: If a mint has HeightEnd set to block 850,000, can a transaction mint at block 850,000?
options: Yes, end height is inclusive
No, end height is strictly exclusive
Yes, if the transaction is confirmed before block 850,001
Only if the cap has not been reached
quiz.explanation: Rule R32 specifies that the end height is exclusive: minting at block height equal to end fails.

title: Plan an Etching
audience: Creators, asset architects, and tooling builders creating new runes.
prerequisites: Understanding of Bitcoin Taproot commitments and confirmation windows.
outcomes: Encode rune names, calculate commitment data pushes, check unlock schedules, and prevent supply overflow.

lessons.title: Name Encoding in Modified Base 26
lessons.summary: A through Z to numeric integer conversion.

lessons.title: The Commit-Reveal Sequence
lessons.summary: Taproot tapscript data push confirmed at least 6 blocks earlier.

lessons.title: Unlock Schedule Milestones
lessons.summary: 13-letter minimum at block 840,000 stepping down to single letters at block 1,050,000.

lessons.title: Divisibility, Symbol, and Spacers
lessons.summary: Formatting rules and maximum allowed ranges.

lessons.title: Supply Overflow Math
lessons.summary: Enforcing premine + cap * amount <= u128::MAX.

quiz.question: How many confirmations must an etching commitment have before the reveal transaction?
options: 1 confirmation
At least 6 confirmations
12 confirmations
No wait is required
quiz.explanation: Rule R28 mandates COMMIT_CONFIRMATIONS = 6: the output spent must be confirmed at least 6 blocks before the etching block.

title: Build a Wallet or Application Integration
audience: Wallet architects, frontend engineers, and Bitcoin backend developers.
prerequisites: TypeScript/JavaScript and Bitcoin transaction serialization experience.
outcomes: Integrate @bitcoinuniverse/runes-tools, manage cardinal inputs, build safe review screens, and prevent balance destruction.

lessons.title: Rune Outpoint Inventory
lessons.summary: Track UTXO rune balances separately to avoid spending rune UTXOs as fee inputs.

lessons.title: Runestone Assembly Pipeline
lessons.summary: Encode edicts, sort by RuneId, calculate minimal varints, and assemble scriptPubKey.

lessons.title: Pre-Signing Validation Gate
lessons.summary: Decode built runestones locally before requesting signatures.

lessons.title: Avoiding Blind Signing
lessons.summary: Surface exact rune amounts, change destination, and burn warnings to users.

quiz.question: Why must a wallet maintain a separate rune outpoint inventory?
options: To display token logos
To prevent rune-bearing UTXOs from being consumed as ordinary fee inputs
To broadcast transactions faster
To bypass the dust limit
quiz.explanation: Rune-unaware coin selection destroys value: spending a rune-bearing UTXO as fee releases its runes into the unallocated pool where they follow output 0.

title: Build or Operate a Runes Indexer
audience: Backend engineers and infrastructure operators indexing Bitcoin blocks.
prerequisites: Bitcoin Core RPC knowledge and relational or key-value storage design.
outcomes: Implement state transitions, handle reorgs via savepoint rewinding, compute allocations, and maintain zero-drift consensus.

lessons.title: Block Processing Sequence
lessons.summary: Process transactions strictly in block order starting from block 840,000.

lessons.title: The Six State Transition Steps
lessons.summary: Gather unallocated, apply mint, apply etching, process edicts, assign remainder, record burns.

lessons.title: Reorg Handling via Savepoint Rollback
lessons.summary: Rewind state on block hash mismatch rather than patching in-place.

lessons.title: Verification Against Test Vectors
lessons.summary: Automate conformance runs against vectors V1-V8 and C1-C14.

quiz.question: How does a conformant Runes indexer handle a blockchain reorganization?
options: By deleting historical blocks and starting from genesis
By rewinding to a confirmed savepoint before the fork and re-indexing forward
By ignoring the reorg if it is under 6 blocks
By mutating balances with delta patches
quiz.explanation: Rune state is derived from the chain. Indexers rewind to a database savepoint before the split and re-index forward using block hashes.
